comment: Rapport does some of what other mods already do, and two mods doing the same
job to the same actor do not add up -- they fight. So Rapport stops their
quests while it owns the feature. Automatic, but never secret: each quest is
checked before it is touched, every change is named in Rapport.log with the
reason, and turning the feature off starts them again. Nothing is deleted and
no file of theirs is modified.
A quest that is already stopped is left alone. A plugin that is not installed
is not an error -- it means there is nothing to take over, and it is still
listed here so that installing it later changes nothing about how Rapport
Stopping a quest is also strictly safer than removing the mod from an active
playthrough: the plugin stays in the load order, so every form it owns still
resolves and no script instance in the save is left pointing at nothing.

entries.reason: Rapport owns persistent aftermath; CumOverlays' own timer removes the same overlay TEMPLATES ours draw from, and would strip them minutes into a twelve-hour window
Rapport replaces Sex 'Em Up; two mods watching for scene opportunities means two mods reserving the same actors, and SEU keeps its own hooks into AAF
Rapport replaces AAF Autonomy Enhanced outright; both would pick pairs and start scenes, and neither would know what the other had reserved
